clue.text: Quite a paper —- now and then!

parts.note: 'quite a' as in 'that was quite a party' means some, as in 'some party'
The Times is the British newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at a fine newspaper, read only occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done sometimes happens occasionally, now and then.

clue.text: Get lost and howl, short of energy

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the word for howl

parts.note: to howl is to scream
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone told to clear off yells, but too tired to do it properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a slang command meaning go away at once, like 'get lost'.

clue.text: States measure up bits of bone for souvenirs

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for measure is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a measure in music is a bar
ilia is the plural of ilium, the hip bone

explanation.surface: Collectors are measuring fragments of bone to sell as keepsakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' gives two abbreviations, ME and MO; 'up' turns BAR to RAB. 'Bits of bone' looks like a clue to fragments, but ILIA are whole bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Memorabilia are objects kept as souvenirs of people or events.

clue.text: Army chap adopting new mathematician's line

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the army-and-chap pair takes a letter inside it

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
a chap is a gent

explanation.surface: A soldier takes on a new view of a mathematician's working.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent is a straight line touching a curve at one point, a term from geometry.

clue.text: Old-fashioned writer gets girl to wash up

parts.note: the writer of the clue, the setter, refers to themself as me
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for wash is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lave is to wash (a literary word)

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned author makes a girl do the washing-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval is used loosely to mean hopelessly out of date or primitive.

clue.text: Bird lives in hide

indicators.note: in places the word for lives inside the word for hide

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin
'is' in the sense of exists, lives

explanation.surface: A bird lives in a birdwatcher's hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' suggests the birdwatcher's shelter, but it is an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch.

clue.text: Woodland plant with neat edge

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a lip is a rim or edge

explanation.surface: A woodland plant has a tidy border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like 'tidy' but is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a primula of damp woods, related to the cowslip and primrose.

clue.text: Dance that was enough for Newman?

definitions.meaning: a ballroom dance popular in the early twentieth century
Cardinal Newman's hymn Lead, Kindly Light says he asks not to see the distant scene, only a single pace ahead

explanation.surface: A dance that satisfied a man named Newman.
explanation.walkthrough: Newman is John Henry Newman, whose hymn 'Lead, Kindly Light' has the line 'I do not ask to see the distant scene; one step enough for me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is a quick ballroom dance done in two-four time.

clue.text: Grassy area providing shelter, by the sound of it

indicators.note: signals that the word for shelter is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A field offers some shelter, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a meadow or pasture, a poetic word.

clue.text: Copper hit out concerning divination

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman strikes out about fortune-telling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the metal or a policeman, but its letters, with HIT, are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Prophetic means relating to prophecy, foretelling the future.

clue.text: Not quite the traveller's type

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Romany describes the Gypsy people, travellers, and their language

explanation.surface: A traveller's kind of thing, almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' is printing type: roman is upright type, as opposed to italic.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman is the ordinary upright typeface used in printing.

clue.text: Reckless person wrongly spared in odd ode

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters of spared inside the rearranged ode
odd means strange, so the letters of ode are rearranged
wrongly signals that spared's letters are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A rash man is mistakenly let off in a strange poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd ode' reads as a strange poem, but 'odd' is an anagram signal like 'wrongly', and each scrambles only the word beside it before one goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw ready for any violence.

clue.text: Horse carries man taking food to wealthy chanteuse

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so the word for horse takes the man's name inside

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
Len is a man's name
diet is the food one eats
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn man brings food to a rich singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was the German-American film star and cabaret singer.

clue.text: Colleague run in on pitch? How untimely

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a colleague or partner
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
being in tune is having the right pitch

explanation.surface: A colleague runs onto the pitch at the wrong moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a sports field; it is musical pitch. In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so TUNE comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Inopportune means coming at a bad time, untimely.

clue.text: Disproof concerning work as head servant, say

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: to buttle is to work as a butler, the head servant

explanation.surface: A rebuttal of claims about being a butler.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a refutation, evidence that disproves a claim.

clue.text: Girl starts to put potion in drink — it bears fruit

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name

indicators.note: in places the two opening letters inside the word for drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer

indicators.note: starts means the first letters of put and potion

explanation.surface: A girl slips a potion into someone's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose apple is a tropical tree grown for its fragrant fruit.

clue.text: Hold forth about right to shoot

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for hold forth goes round the letter

parts.note: to spout is to hold forth, talk at length

explanation.surface: Someone sounds off about their right to fire a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' suggests firing; it is a young plant growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprout is a new shoot on a plant.

clue.text: Accompanied piece finally orchestrated? About time

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of piece
about means around, so the word for orchestrated goes round the letter

parts.note: a piece scored for an orchestra has been orchestrated

explanation.surface: A piece of music, at last orchestrated, took its time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accompanied' suggests music, but here it means went along with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to accompany them.

clue.text: A line in function leads to solution

indicators.note: in puts A and the line abbreviation inside the trigonometric function

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A line inside a mathematical function leads to the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' looks like a maths answer but is a liquid mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Saline is a solution of salt in water, used medically.

clue.text: One's injured, having landed on hard stone artefact

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters of one are knocked out of shape

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
lit means landed, as a bird lit on a branch
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone is hurt after landing on something hard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so H comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A neolith is a stone implement from the New Stone Age.

clue.text: Nothing in one's subject is like some atoms

indicators.note: in places the zero letter between the two following parts

parts.note: I is one, so one's gives I and S
a topic is a subject
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is in someone's chosen subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopic means relating to isotopes, atoms of one element differing in mass.

clue.text: Overwhelmed by drink, wife stole powerful vessel

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means engulfed, so the word for drink goes around the others

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits
a boa is a feather or fur stole

explanation.surface: A drunk wife made off with a powerful boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like the verb for theft; it is a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A towboat is a powerful boat used for towing or pushing barges.

clue.text: Heavy metal thus upset parent, one admitted

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for thus upside down

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the parent takes the letter inside

parts.note: mum is a parent
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A heavy metal fan thus upsets a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' suggests rock music, but means a dense element.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element, a metal.

clue.text: Unlike a lexicographer, not knowing what to say

definitions.meaning: a dictionary maker has no shortage of vocabulary

explanation.surface: Someone, unlike a dictionary writer, cannot find anything to say.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: a lexicographer is never short of vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means speechless, unable to think what to say.

clue.text: Ultimately victorious players may let it off

definitions.text: Ultimately victorious players may let it off

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of victorious

parts.note: players make up a team

explanation.surface: Winning players celebrate by relaxing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: winners 'let off steam', release pent-up feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off steam is the idiom for releasing tension, which victorious teams do.

clue.text: Press agent's son allowed to go round behind bar

indicators.note: behind means coming after the word for bar

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: the word for allowed goes round the letter for son

parts.note: licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: A press agent's son is allowed into a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A publicist promotes clients in the press, a publicity agent.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval in bachelor circles

parts.note: O is a circle, so two make OO

explanation.surface: A bachelor's social circles show disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Boo is a jeer of disapproval.

clue.text: Body in plant representing universal love?

indicators.note: representing taken as re-presenting, the letters set out afresh

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A plant symbolises universal love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' suggests O for zero, but here it is anagram fodder with U.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovule is the structure in a plant's ovary that becomes a seed.

clue.text: Old church record taking precedence for a long time

indicators.note: taking precedence means coming first, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An old church register takes priority for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period of history or geology.

clue.text: Current position from which banks remain equally distanced

definitions.text: Current position from which banks remain equally distanced

parts.words: Current position from which banks remain equally distanced
parts.note: the current is a river's flow, and the banks are its sides, each the same distance away

explanation.surface: Like a financial status keeping banks at arm's length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present' and 'banks' like financial firms; they are a river's flow and its sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Midstream is the middle of a river, equidistant from both banks.
